neighbours.label: The marker of a second item in an enumeration or pair ('(2)', 'G' in 'A-T and G-C', 'Second,'): the slot where a list moves to its next member
fire: The grant has two aims: (1) to train new nurses and (2) to build a clinic.
Students must (a) read the chapter and (b) answer the questions at the end.
The theory makes two claims: (1) prices rise slowly and (2) wages follow later.
Applicants need (1) a passport photo and (2) a copy of their birth certificate.
The report shows that (i) costs fell and (ii) customer complaints doubled.
Two problems remain: (1) the roof leaks and (2) the heating is broken.
In the code, bases pair as A with T and C with G.
The study had two goals: (1) to map the river and (2) to count the fish.
quiet: The grant has one aim: to train new nurses for the rural clinic.
Students must read the chapter carefully before the next class.
The theory makes one claim: prices rise slowly over many years.
Applicants need a passport photo taken within the last month.
The report shows that costs fell sharply over the past year.
One problem remains: the roof still leaks when it rains hard.
In the code, each base is written as a single capital letter.
The study had one goal: to map the river from source to sea.

predictions: '(2)' in an inline numbered list and second members of letter pairs reach 0.3-0.8; the same sentences with a single unnumbered item stay under 0.05.
notes: Probe: '(1) short ... and (2) long ones' 0.838, 'A-T and G-C' 0.466, 'Second, it raises' 0.248, 'and the other on offshore islands' 0.203, 'the second focused' 0.169, 'points A and B' 0.095; single-item controls 0.018-0.024. The inline '(2)' frame is strongest, so most fire items use it.
